item.title: Thus, bhikkhus, the Tathāgata has seen what is to be seen, but he does not conceive what is seen, does not conceive what is not…
item.description:
Thus, bhikkhus, the Tathāgata has seen what is to be seen, but he does not conceive what is seen, does not conceive what is not seen, does not conceive what is to be seen, does not conceive a seer. He has heard what is to be heard, but he does not conceive what is heard, does not conceive what is not heard, does not conceive what is to be heard, does not conceive a hearer. He has sensed what is to be sensed, but he does not conceive what is sensed, does not conceive what is not sensed, does not conceive what is to be sensed, does not conceive a senser. He has cognized what is to be cognized, but he does not conceive what is cognized, does not conceive what is not cognized, does not conceive what is to be cognized, does not conceive a cognizer. Thus, bhikkhus, the Tathāgata, regarding phenomena that are seen, heard, sensed, and cognized, is just thus. Moreover, beyond one who is thus, there is no one else more excellent or superior. So I declare.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 4.24

item.title: Kevaddha, hearing this, I said to that bhikkhu: 'Bhikkhu, in the past, sea-merchants when sailing across the ocean would take along a land-sighting bird. When…
item.description:
Kevaddha, hearing this, I said to that bhikkhu: 'Bhikkhu, in the past, sea-merchants when sailing across the ocean would take along a land-sighting bird. When the ship had sailed far out and land was no longer visible, the merchants would release the land-sighting bird. The bird would fly east, south, west, north, upwards, and in intermediate directions. If it saw land all around, it would fly towards that land. If it did not see land all around, it would return to the ship. So too, bhikkhu, you have searched as far as the Brahmā realm without finding an answer to that question, so you have returned to me. Bhikkhu, the question should not be asked thus: "Venerable Sir, where do the four great elements — earth, water, fire, air — go after they have completely ceased?" Bhikkhu, the question should be asked thus: "Where do earth, water, fire, and air, long and short, fine and coarse, pure and impure, find no footing? Where do name-and-form completely cease?" And this is the answer to that question:

Consciousness is invisible, boundless, all-pervasive.
Here, earth, water, fire, wind element find no footing.
Here, also, long and short, fine and coarse, pure and impure.
Here, name and form completely cease.
When consciousness ceases, here everything ceases utterly.

From: Dīgha Nikāya 11 – Kevaṭṭasutta

item.title: Bhikkhus, what is Right Speech? Refraining from false speech, refraining from divisive speech, refraining from harsh speech, refraining from idle chatter. Bhikkhus, this is called…
item.description:
Bhikkhus, what is Right Speech? Refraining from false speech, refraining from divisive speech, refraining from harsh speech, refraining from idle chatter. Bhikkhus, this is called Right Speech.

From: Dīgha Nikāya 22 – Mahāsatipaṭṭhānasutta

item.title: Speak with a person Who has a sword in hand, Speak with a demon, Or sit very close. A snake with venom, If bitten, death…
item.description:
Speak with a person
Who has a sword in hand,
Speak with a demon,
Or sit very close.
A snake with venom,
If bitten, death follows,
But never alone
Speak with a woman.
Unmindful, they bind you
With glances, with smiles,
With loose garments,
With sweet words.
That person still unsatisfied,
Confused, meets death.
Those five nurturing sensual pleasures
Are seen in female form:
Forms, sounds, scents, tastes, touches,
Alluring and delightful.
By the waterfall of sensual desires,
Flooded and swept away,
The foolish, unwise person
Does not understand sensual pleasures.
Humans, upon death,
Realm of existence or non-existence,
They are led along
Through many rounds of rebirth.
One who understands sensual pleasures,
Whose conduct is fearless,
They reach the further shore,
Attain the destruction of taints.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 5.55

item.title: Here, bhikkhus, a person has not attained internal serenity of mind and has not attained the higher wisdom of insight into phenomena. That person, bhikkhus,…
item.description:
Here, bhikkhus, a person has not attained internal serenity of mind and has not attained the higher wisdom of insight into phenomena. That person, bhikkhus, should approach someone who has attained internal serenity of mind and the higher wisdom of insight into phenomena and say to him: 'Friend, how should the mind be established? How should the mind be settled? How should the mind be unified? How should the mind be concentrated? How should formations be seen? How should formations be known? How should formations be contemplated?' That person answers him: 'As has been seen, as has been known, thus, friend, should the mind be established; thus should the mind be settled; thus should the mind be unified; thus should the mind be concentrated; thus should formations be seen; thus should formations be known; thus should formations be contemplated.' After some time, that person attains internal serenity of mind and attains the higher wisdom of insight into phenomena. Then, bhikkhus, this person, after establishing himself in those wholesome states, should focus on training for the destruction of the taints.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 4.94

item.title: Elder Cūḷagavaccha: A bhikkhu of great joy in the Dhamma proclaimed by the Buddha, Attains the peaceful state — the bliss of peace of all…
item.description:
Elder Cūḷagavaccha:

A bhikkhu of great joy in the Dhamma proclaimed by the Buddha,
Attains the peaceful state — the bliss of peace of all conditioned things.

From: Theragāthā 1.11

item.title: These four things, bhikkhus, are true, not false, not otherwise. What four? 'This is suffering,' bhikkhus, is true, not false, not otherwise. 'This is the…
item.description:
These four things, bhikkhus, are true, not false, not otherwise. What four? 'This is suffering,' bhikkhus, is true, not false, not otherwise. 'This is the origin of suffering,' bhikkhus, is true, not false, not otherwise. 'This is the cessation of suffering,' bhikkhus, is true, not false, not otherwise. 'This is the path leading to the cessation of suffering,' bhikkhus, is true, not false, not otherwise. These four things, bhikkhus, are true, not false, not otherwise. Therefore, bhikkhus, an exertion should be made to understand: 'This is suffering.' ... an exertion should be made to understand: 'This is the path leading to the cessation of suffering.'

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 56.20

item.title: Almsfood, lodging, a place to sit, water for washing, And the outer robe — after hearing the Dhamma taught by the Well-Gone One, A wise…
item.description:
Almsfood, lodging, a place to sit, water for washing,
And the outer robe — after hearing the Dhamma taught by the Well-Gone One,
A wise disciple, having reflected, should use them.

Therefore, almsfood, lodging, water for washing, and the outer robe —
Do not become attached to these things.
A bhikkhu, like a water drop on a lotus leaf, should not cling.

From: Sutta Nipāta 2.14

item.title: Elder Jotidāsa: Those who use ropes, who rob in various ways, Those cruel people who harm others — Thus they cause harm, because kamma does…
item.description:
Elder Jotidāsa:

Those who use ropes, who rob in various ways,
Those cruel people who harm others —
Thus they cause harm, because kamma does not vanish.

Whatever kamma one does, good or evil,
One is the heir of that kamma, of the kamma one is doing.

From: Theragāthā 2.12

item.title: And, bhikkhus, how does a bhikkhu not fumigate? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu does not teach the Dhamma extensively to others as he has heard and…
item.description:
And, bhikkhus, how does a bhikkhu not fumigate? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu does not teach the Dhamma extensively to others as he has heard and learned it. Thus, bhikkhus, is a bhikkhu who does not fumigate. And, bhikkhus, how does a bhikkhu not know the ford? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu does not from time to time approach those bhikkhus who are learned, who have received the tradition of the scriptures, who are experts in the Dhamma, experts in the Discipline, experts in the summaries; he does not ask them, does not question them: 'How is this, venerable sir? What is the meaning of this?' Those venerable ones do not reveal what is unrevealed, do not clarify what is unclear, and regarding various points of Dhamma, they do not remove doubt. Thus, bhikkhus, is a bhikkhu who does not know the ford. And, bhikkhus, how does a bhikkhu not know the drinking place? Here, bhikkhus, when the Dhamma and Discipline proclaimed by the Tathāgata is being taught, he does not attain the meaning of faith, the Dhamma of faith, does not attain gladness connected with the Dhamma. Thus, bhikkhus, is a bhikkhu who does not know the drinking place.

From: Majjhima Nikāya 33 – Mahāgopālakasutta
